title: fix: harden Z-Image Vast startup
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Keeps new workers local-only until an explicit persistent tunnel-enable marker is created.
- Waits for local Z-Image health before joining the shared production Cloudflare Tunnel.
- Adds a conditional, reboot-safe DNS-over-HTTPS fallback for Vast hosts that drop required SRV responses.
- Uses the empirically verified PyPI CUDA 12.8/Blackwell wheel path and documents the current Vast fleet, cost, limits, and canary results.
- Does not change credentials, encrypted secrets, registry pricing, or production routing.

Validation:
- `bash -n image.pollinations.ai/z-image/setup-vast.sh`
- Extracted generated `/root/onstart.sh` parses with `bash -n`
- `git diff --check`
- Live canary: 102/102 successful at concurrency 4 over 120s; 4.69s p50, 5.73s p95; reboot and production soak passed.

gist.headline: New bees join quietly
gist.blurb: Z-Image workers now finish their little local health check before joining the big production tunnel. The canary made 102 out of 102 images without dropping a petal.
gist.summary: Hardened Z-Image Vast startup so new GPU workers stay local until explicitly tunnel-enabled, verify local health before joining the production Cloudflare Tunnel, and use a reboot-safe DNS-over-HTTPS fallback when Vast hosts omit required SRV responses.
gist.impact: Users gain more reliable Z-Image capacity: the live Vast canary completed 102/102 requests at concurrency 4 with 4.69s p50 and 5.73s p95 latency, including reboot and production-soak validation.
